figures.label: 圖一
figures.caption: 圖一：校門口的全班團體照
figures.description: 校門口，全班三十多位同學穿著整齊的制服排成三排，前排蹲著、後排站著，導師坐在第一排中間，大家面向鏡頭微笑；攝影師站在前方的三腳架後面，舉手示意大家看鏡頭。

questions.stem: 提示：高三畢業前，同學們常在校園各處拍照留念。請仔細看下面兩張圖片，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種畢業照有什麼不同；第二段寫出你自己和同學拍照留念的一次經驗，並說明你比較喜歡哪一種畢業照及原因。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段比較兩種畢業照（圖一在校門口、全班排整齊、正式；圖二在教室、幾個好友自拍、輕鬆搞笑），要寫出差異而不是各描述一次；第二段寫一次自己和同學拍照留念的經驗，再說明比較喜歡哪一種畢業照與原因。兩種都可以選，理由要和經驗連起來。
evidence: 比較圖一與圖二兩種畢業照有什麼不同
說明你比較喜歡哪一種畢業照及原因
1.strategy_zh: 比較時可以從地點、人數、姿勢、氣氛四個方面對照，用 however、on the other hand 連接；第二段先寫拍照經驗，再表態並給理由，最後也可以承認另一種的優點。
hints: 第一段：In Picture 1, … In Picture 2, however, … 寫出地點、人數、氣氛的不同
第二段：Last …, my classmates and I took photos … 寫一次拍照經驗
用 I like … better because … 說明偏好，結尾回應題目

content.focus_zh: 第一段要比較兩張圖的地點、人數與氣氛；第二段要有一次具體的拍照經驗，並說明比較喜歡哪一種畢業照與理由。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段用對比的轉承語把兩張圖放在一起比較；第二段的偏好要呼應第一段提到的差異，結尾回到畢業照的意義。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 圖片用現在進行式，經驗用過去式；suggest that 後面接原形動詞（everyone jump）；比較級 better than 要完整。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 畢業、制服、團體照、自拍等說法（graduation、uniform、class photo、take a photo of themselves）要用對；避免一直重複 funny 和 happy。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

sentence_starters: Last ..., my classmates and I took photos ...

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two different kinds of graduation photos. In Picture 1, the whole class is standing in three neat rows in front of the school gate. The students in the front row are squatting, and their teacher is sitting in the middle. Everyone is wearing the school uniform and smiling at the camera. In Picture 2, however, four close friends are taking a photo of themselves in their classroom. One boy is wearing a pair of funny glasses, and a girl is making a heart with her hands. Behind them, the blackboard is covered with their names.
Last June, my classmates and I took photos together after our school sports day. At first, we stood in a line and smiled politely, but the photos looked boring. Then my friend suggested that everyone jump at the same time. We tried five times, and finally we got a photo with all of us in the air. I like the funny kind of graduation photo better because it shows our real personalities. For example, when I look at that jumping photo, I can still hear our laughter. Still, a class photo is important, since it includes everyone. To sum up, I hope to take both kinds of photos before I graduate, but the funny ones will always be my favorites.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
Both pictures capture the same moment, graduation, yet they tell two very different stories. Picture 1 is a traditional class photo: more than thirty students in neat uniforms are standing in three straight rows at the school gate, with their homeroom teacher seated in the center of the front row. A photographer behind a tripod is signaling everyone to look at the lens, and every face wears the same polite smile. Picture 2, on the other hand, is pure chaos in the best sense. Squeezed in front of a blackboard covered with signatures, four close friends are taking a selfie. One boy is wearing giant novelty glasses, a girl is forming a heart with her hands, and another boy is pretending to write on the board. Whereas the first photo records who was there, the second records what it felt like to be there.
Last spring, my friends and I tried to take both kinds of photos on our last day of eleventh grade. The formal one took almost twenty minutes, because someone always blinked or looked away just as the shutter clicked. After that, we squeezed together for a quick selfie. Ironically, that spontaneous one took only a few seconds, but it has become the picture I treasure most. In it, my best friend is laughing so hard that her eyes have disappeared, and I am holding a paper sign with our class number on it. Admittedly, a formal class photo has its own value. Years from now, it will be the only record that includes every single classmate, even the shy ones who never joined our jokes. Nevertheless, I prefer the playful kind, since memories are made of feelings rather than neat rows. All in all, every graduating class should ideally take both, one for the yearbook and one for the heart.
